papers.title: Embedded sensing telemetry and a validated explicit finite element digital twin of pressurised uPVC pipe under low velocity impact
papers.abstract: Polymeric pipelines are increasingly used for pressurized fluid transport, yet their behavior under accidental low-velocity impact, and the means to monitor it in service, remain underdeveloped relative to metallic systems. This study recasts a combined experimental and numerical investigation of clamped unplasticized poly(vinyl chloride) (uPVC) pipe as the first building block of a physics-based digital twin for polymeric utility pipelines. A drop-weight rig was instrumented with a purpose-built ESP32-S2 sensing unit, using infrared timing gates and a pressure transducer, that streams real impact telemetry: the hammer velocity and the transient internal pressure pulse. Five water-pressurized specimens, spanning 689.48 to 2068.43 kPa, were struck at mid-span by a 4 kg hammer at 5.56 m/s, and a high-fidelity ABAQUS/Explicit counterpart was synchronized against the measured response. As internal pressure rose, the peak contact force increased from 3527 to 4174 N, the permanent deformation fell from 15.1 to 7.0 mm, and the pressure pulse grew while the contact period shortened, all consistent with pressure-induced wall stiffening. The contact-force response was linear up to about 1379 kPa before plateauing at the onset of the burst-pressure regime. Experimental and numerical plastic-zone areas agreed to within 16.9%, a conservative over-prediction the twin corrects during synchronization. On this validated basis, a conceptual digital-twin framework is proposed, enabling real-time damage identification and predictive, surrogate-driven structural health monitoring of polymeric pipelines.

papers.title: STEM faculty perception of student resistance as a source of faculty's self‐efficacy
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Despite decades of reform efforts, lecture remains the dominant mode of instruction in undergraduate engineering education. Faculty often cite student resistance to active learning as a barrier to instructional change. However, little research has examined how faculty perceptions of such resistance influence their motivation and instructional practices. Purpose/Hypothesis(es) Guided by Social Cognitive Theory, this study investigates how faculty perceptions and students' self‐reported resistance influence faculty self‐efficacy and the adoption of active learning instructional practices. Design/Method This longitudinal study involved 173 STEM faculty and 1649 students across 64 U.S. institutions. Faculty completed surveys at three time points over two terms; students completed surveys at the middle time point after an active learning session. Latent change score modeling was used to examine the relations between faculty self‐efficacy, instructional practice, and resistance. Results Faculty self‐efficacy at the start of the semester predicted increased use of active learning. Faculty perceptions of student resistance partially mediated this relation, while student‐reported resistance did not. Students' self‐reported resistance was higher in engineering than in other disciplines. Overall, faculty perceptions of student resistance were only weakly related to student reports; however, this relation may be much stronger within engineering courses. Conclusions Faculty self‐efficacy for approaches to teaching that focus on active learning and perceptions of student resistance to active learning play a significant role in shaping instructional practices. To support a broader adoption of active learning in engineering education, professional development should target self‐efficacy for using active learning and strategies to reduce student resistance.

papers.title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution‐inspired multi‐objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active‐learning framework that integrates path‐dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi‐objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high‐value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state‐of‐the‐art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA‐binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target‐region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two‐ and three‐objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation‐derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme‐engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus , probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non‐native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae , stability‐related descriptors identified aggregation‐resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi‐objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism‐derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

papers.title: Le scuole sperimentali italiane e il modello giapponese di Tomoe Gakuen: un confronto pedagogico tra educazione attiva, personalizzazione e comunità educante
papers.abstract: This article examines comparatively the main Italian experimental and alternative educational models — including Montessori education, Reggio Emilia approach, Waldorf/Steiner schools, and other active learning experiences — in relation to the Japanese educational experience of Tomoe Gakuen, founded by Sōsaku Kobayashi in the 1930s. The study aims to identify pedagogical convergences and divergences concerning the concepts of child-centered education, experiential learning, educational freedom, personalization, relational pedagogy, and the role of the educational environment. Through a historical-comparative and pedagogical analysis, the paper highlights how Tomoe Gakuen represented an innovative educational experience within the Japanese context, anticipating several contemporary educational themes such as inclusion, holistic development, emotional well-being, interdisciplinarity, and community-based education. The article also investigates the different epistemological foundations underlying these educational models: scientific pedagogy in Montessori education, socio-constructivist and democratic perspectives in the Reggio Emilia approach, spiritual-anthroposophical principles in Waldorf education, and the humanistic-experiential orientation characterizing Tomoe Gakuen. The comparative framework demonstrates that, despite cultural and historical differences, these educational experiences share a common critique of traditional authoritarian schooling and promote an integral vision of human development centered on the dignity, autonomy, and uniqueness of the child. Finally, the study reflects on the contemporary relevance of these pedagogical paradigms in addressing current educational challenges related to standardization, student well-being, and inclusive schooling.

papers.title: Impact of Heat‐Treatment‐Induced Microstructural Evolution on the High‐Temperature Wear and Corrosion Resistance of L‐PBF Scalmalloy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The high‐temperature (HT) tribological and corrosion performance of Scalmalloy produced via laser powder bed fusion (L‐PBF) remains insufficiently uncharacterized despite its growing adoption in many industrial applications. This study examines the impact of post‐heat treatment (325°C for 4 h) on the microstructure, nano‐hardness, room‐temperature (RT) and HT tribological behavior and corrosion resistance of the alloy. Microstructural characterization revealed that heat treatment conserved the bimodal microstructure achieved in the L‐PBF process, while improving the homogenous distribution of coherent Al 3 (Sc,Zr) nanoprecipitates, as evidenced by x‐ray diffraction analysis. The coherent nanoparticles restricted the localized plastic deformation by inhibiting the movement of dislocations, thus enhancing the nano‐hardness. The refined precipitate distribution enhanced the nano‐indentation hardness from 3.50 ± 0.10 to 4.26 ± 0.11 GPa, resulting in an improved wear resistance. During reciprocating sliding, the Post‐Heat‐Treated (PHT) Scalmalloy exhibited lower friction coefficient, wear volume loss, and specific wear rate compared to that of As‐Printed (ASP) alloy. With 200°C test temperature, the wear rate was dropped to 39.23%, which was due to the precipitation of Al 3 (Sc,Zr) and the formation of an oxide tribo‐layer. Corrosion resistance was also superior, with the PHT specimen achieving a corrosion rate of 0.3809 mpy at RT and lower weight loss under HT corrosion compared to the ASP condition.

papers.title: Hybrid Mathematical-PINN Model for Tumor-Immune Interaction with Holling Type-II Functional Response and Optimal Control
papers.abstract: Code accompanying the article “Hybrid Mathematical-PINN Model for Tumor-Immune Interaction with Holling Type-II Functional Response and Optimal Control”. The package reproduces the dynamical-systems results for the three-variable tumor, hunting-cell and resting-cell model with Holling Type-II responses and tumor-induced immune suppression (baseline parameters of Table 2, μd = 0.05). It contains the RK4 reference solution; the exact analysis of the interior equilibria, including the quintic coexistence condition, the saddle-node bifurcation near w2 = 0.4385 and a count of admissible equilibria over the parameter ranges studied; the Sotomayor conditions for the transcritical bifurcation of the hunting-cell-free equilibrium; the Hopf point and first Lyapunov coefficient; and the regenerated bifurcation diagram (Figure 4) with its limit-cycle envelope. A verification folder holds independent re-implementations of a forward–backward sweep for the Pontryagin optimal-control problem and of a state-only physics-informed neural network, with analytic gradients checked against finite differences. [Scripts used for Figures 1–3 and 5–9 and Table 6 are in the folder.] This version updates the earlier deposit to match the revised article. The code is written in Python (NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, mpmath, Matplotlib); the README gives the run order, expected outputs and run times.
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
